disposition_reason: Twenty samples each of 20 vegetables bought at a Dhaka market were analysed for total arsenic, inorganic arsenic, MMA and DMA by ion-exchange separation and silver diethyldithiocarbamate colorimetry; Table I prints range and mean ± SD per vegetable.

study.design: Market survey with arsenic speciation and phosphate correlation
study.market: A local market of Dhaka city, Bangladesh
study.method: 50% methanol extraction, cation-exchange (AG 50W-X8) separation of inorganic arsenic, MMA and DMA, silver diethyldithiocarbamate (SDDC) colorimetry at 525 nm
study.qa: no reference material or recovery data reported

unresolved: Table I has no unit; the Results text gives the same values mostly in ug/g but prints some inorganic arsenic values as mg/g, and Table II labels total arsenic in mg/g. Values were recorded as ug/g following the majority of the text; mg/g would be implausible.

Basis not labelled; vegetables were washed, surface dried and frozen, so values are taken as fresh weight. Mean total arsenic of 2-4 ug/g fresh weight is high for vegetables; the colorimetric method has no stated detection limit or quality control.
Range lower bounds printed 0.0 are recorded as not detected without a detection limit.
Table II quartile-group arsenic means (tomato, lady's finger and others) are sub-analyses of the same samples and were not recorded. Inorganic phosphate values are not metal findings.
